issues.detail: The Greek 'πραθηναι' (to be sold) is rendered as 'bán được nhiều tiền' (can be sold for a lot of money). The Greek does not specify 'nhiều tiền' (a lot of money); it simply says 'πολλου' (much/many), which in this context refers to the quantity of the oil being sold or the extent of the sale, not necessarily the monetary value.

The Greek 'δοθηναι' is a passive infinitive (to be given). The Vietnamese 'đem cho' (bring to/give to) is active. While often acceptable, in the context of 'sold and given,' the Greek implies a sequence of being sold [by many] and being given [to the poor].
